transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-05-12
Time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~1h7m
Location: Zoom - internal

Attendees: Jamie Liu, Sanjay Patel, Marta Gomez, Oliver Chen, Leah Brooks, Priya Nair, Evan Park, Rita Alvarez, Connor Mills

---
Summary (auto): sketching surge scenarios and slice triage. identify observability gaps. assign runbook and QA owners.
---

00:00 Jamie Liu: okay, hey everyone thanks for joining, we'll kick off in about 1 minute, couple of late folks pinged in the chat but looks like we're green to go
00:18 Sanjay Patel: cool, yeah quick context, this is tied to the private beta for customer X, they've got spiky traffic profile — websocket bursts + steady backlog, we need to define what we tolerate and what's the slice order if we have to drop capacity
00:35 Marta Gomez: just to clarify, by slices we mean lane-level features? e.g., embeddings heavy, chat streaming, and then reranking?
00:50 Sanjay Patel: yep, exactly, plus background batch embeddings which we can shift to cheaper q8 / quantized nodes if needed
01:06 Leah Brooks: and remember compliance lane for enterprise customers — that slice can't be degraded without legal signoff, so it should be last-resort
01:25 Priya Nair: last-resort but we flagged that private deployment will have per-tenant isolation, so we could have tenant-level degrade policy, not global — worth planning both
01:42 Jamie Liu: right. first agenda item: enumerate plausible surge scenarios. Sanjay, you had three sketches?
01:55 Sanjay Patel: yup. scenario A: traffic spike for 10-15 minutes from a PLG event — high qps, short lived. scenario B: sustained 2x qps for 3 hours due to misconfigured job. scenario C: gradual memory leak causing node oom over 6-12 hours causing capacity drop and sequential fallbacks
02:20 Evan Park: for A we can rely on burst capacity if we allow preemption across lower-priority slices, but that means instantaneous latency hits for those lanes
02:38 Rita Alvarez: from QA side, we need a defined SLICE smoke test that runs in <3m so we can detect functional regressions when we flip slices — current smoke is 12m which is too long for canary reaction
02:55 Connor Mills: ops note — our autoscaler currently scales on CPU and GPU util, but pinning to tail latency will require trace changes, doesn't exist in staging yet
03:15 Sanjay Patel: that ties into observability gaps. I wanted to show a quick slide but I'll just call out: KV cache eviction traces don't show prefix-level hits, so when we evict prefix we don't know which models or routes were most impacted
03:38 Oliver Chen: yes this is one of the big blindspots. when we do continuous batching we rely on KV cache hits to preserve latency; if we can't attribute evictions to slices we can't make a safe degrade decision
03:55 Jamie Liu: let's put that as high priority, Sanjay — can you instrument per-slice eviction metrics?
04:04 Sanjay Patel: yes I think so, will need a small agent change, low risk. I'll aim for staging deploy by Tue next week
04:18 Marta Gomez: next, ordering/prioritization. propose matrix: customer priority (compliance > SLA-paid > free), cost delta (units/token cost to run slice), and fragility (how fragile is slice to quantization/batching). Let's walk through an example
04:38 Leah Brooks: we should include feature flags and canary tags in the matrix so we can do partial degrade — e.g., turn off streaming for low tiers but keep sync short completion for paid tiers
04:54 Priya Nair: also consider data residency lane — that one is pinned to private nodes in region, so capacity decisions there are different
05:10 Jamie Liu: okay, can we sketch a recommended first-cut order? Marta?
05:18 Marta Gomez: rough proposal: 1) background batch embeddings (cheapest to move to q8/cheaper infra), 2) free-tier streaming (degrade to buffered responses), 3) reranking/low-priority LLM routes, 4) paid-tier streaming (only if severe), 5) compliance/resident workloads last
05:40 Connor Mills: that seems reasonable. concern: stepping from 2->3 will change token mix and could spike cost; need to simulate token-distribution changes
05:52 Sanjay Patel: we can run a synthetic replay with amplified traffic to estimate token delta; I can run two replays — one for 2x sustained and one for 5x short spike
06:09 Rita Alvarez: QA gating: I'll need clear pass/fail criteria: smoke, latency tail under threshold, and functional tests for degrade modes. Also, rollback criteria if errors > X% in 15m window
06:28 Oliver Chen: and we need a rollforward checklist: i) identify failing slice, ii) reduce concurrency / shed load, iii) enable cheaper quantized variant, iv) if still degraded, start controlled traffic shedding per-priority matrix, v) communicate to console and customers
06:47 Jamie Liu: communication piece — Leah, can you draft the console messaging templates? we need in-product banners and webhook notification payloads for tenants
06:58 Leah Brooks: yea I can draft two: urgent and advisory formats, will share as a PR for review by tomorrow EOD
07:07 Sanjay Patel: quick note on model variants — fallback to quantized or smaller families only safe if we run eval sets; we should predefine eval pass thresholds before we flip automatically
07:24 Marta Gomez: put that in the runbook: precondition check list includes eval set pass rate > 95% for top-level intents, and manual override if below
07:38 Priya Nair: observability implementation detail — we also need end-to-end synthetic agents that assert correctness across degraded slices, not just latency. We'll craft a small scenario runner
07:52 Connor Mills: ops/infra: for private beta we have two cluster pools, one for compliance and one for standard; should we allow cross-pool burst? my vote is no, to avoid noisy neighbor risk
08:06 Oliver Chen: agree, but we can enable controlled cross-pool burst as a last resort with explicit gating and tenant consent
08:17 Jamie Liu: ok those are design decisions. Let's capture required telemetry changes: per-slice eviction trace, tail-latency buckets, token-mix deltas during degrade, and alerting thresholds wired to paging
08:36 Sanjay Patel: I'll open a tracking ticket with the three telemetry tasks and link to staging PRs
08:45 Rita Alvarez: on the tabletop drill — propose 30 minutes: 10m scenario readout, 10m run through rollforward steps, 10m retro and adjust runbook. Keep it lightweight. 24th works for me
08:58 Marta Gomez: timeline: we need runbook skeleton by 19th to then run tabletop 24th and iterate; aligns with customer beta by end of month
09:12 Jamie Liu: objections? anyone think we're missing something big?
09:18 Evan Park: only that we should stress test with mixed workloads (embeddings + chat + rerank concurrently) — single-slice tests aren't representative
09:30 Connor Mills: plus we need to validate autoscaler thresholds so we don't thrash nodes during short-lived spikes
09:41 Jamie Liu: great. recap of owners: Oliver runbook, Sanjay traces, Rita QA, Marta prioritization matrix, Leah console messages, Jamie capacity cost spreadsheet. we'll reconvene next Wed for status and if PRs land earlier we'll update the doc
09:58 Jamie Liu: any last words?
10:03 Sanjay Patel: small nit — add a toggle in runtime to pause automatic fallback for certain tenants during canary, so we can observe behavior before flipping it on globally
10:19 Jamie Liu: noted. thanks everyone. I'll post the recording in the internal channel and create Git issue links for action items
10:30 Meeting ends
